title: A galactic disc, edge-on and up close
caption: Part of the disc of the Needle Galaxy, NGC 4565, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4565 · constellation Coma Berenices · about 40 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Ribbons of dust cross the bright disc of the spiral galaxy NGC 4565 in this detailed Hubble close-up. At lower right, the dust stands out even more sharply against the rich yellow light of the star-filled central regions. The galaxy's core lies just out of frame in that direction.

NGC 4565 is one of the most famous edge-on spirals, turned so that we look straight into its glowing disc. Viewed whole, it shows up as a thin sliver of light, which has earned it the nickname the Needle Galaxy.

This edgewise view is much like our own view from the Solar System toward the core of the Milky Way, where dust also blocks part of the disc's light. At only about 40 million light-years away, the galaxy is fairly close, and it is big, roughly one third larger than the Milky Way. That makes it useful for comparing with our home.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.34 x 2.64 arcminutes) and distance (40 million light years), the frame spans roughly 39,000 × 31,000 light-years. Its light set out about 40 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, using visible and near-infrared filters. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Part of the data is near-infrared light, invisible to the eye, and this level of detail is far beyond naked-eye or small-telescope views.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The image was taken with Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and spans about 3.4 by 3.4 arcminutes. Josh Barrington entered a version of it in Hubble's Hidden Treasures image processing competition.
alt: A close-up of an edge-on galaxy disc crossed by dark ribbons of dust, with yellow light from the central regions at lower right.
